```{r setup, include=FALSE}
has_sce <- requireNamespace("SingleCellExperiment", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = has_sce)
```

The optional `SingleCellExperiment` interface imports one complete raw response
assay and one guide alternative experiment. It follows the raw UMI and ordered
cell requirements in the
[SCEPTRE book](https://timothy-barry.github.io/sceptre-book/import-data.html).
Install `SingleCellExperiment` separately with BiocManager if needed. Ordinary
SCEPTRE import and external assignments work without this optional package.

Start with the complete unnormalized feature library. Import computes library
size, detected-feature counts, and (with gene names) mitochondrial fractions
from all supplied response features, before selecting test pairs or running QC.
An SCE filtered upstream has already lost that information: this interface
cannot
recover original library depths. Do not pass a first feature subset as though
it
were the full library. No normalization, imputation, feature filtering, cell
matching, or disk-assay realization occurs here. Dense numeric and dgC/dgR/dgT
sparse raw-count assays are supported. Convert delayed assays explicitly only
after checking the required memory.

```{r import-sce}
library(sceptre)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
data("lowmoi_example_data")
x <- lowmoi_example_data
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = x$response_matrix),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(x$extra_covariates))
altExp(sce, "gRNA") <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = x$grna_matrix))
object <- import_from_sce(sce, x$grna_target_data_frame, "low",
    covariates = "batch")
```

Response features, guide features and cells need unique, nonempty IDs. Guide
metadata must describe every guide in exactly its assay row order. Selected
`colData` columns become additional covariates; unselected columns remain on
the
SCE. Named physical assays and the unmodified guide alternative experiment must
also agree with their container IDs; SCE's default name overlay cannot hide a
stored permutation. Unnamed physical assays use their container's explicit IDs,
whose original ordering remains the constructing caller's responsibility.
To compute mitochondrial fractions from symbols rather than feature IDs,
name a `rowData` column using `response_name_column`. Use the `counts` assay,
never `logcounts`, size-factor-adjusted counts, or an embedding. Integer-valued
normalized data cannot be identified automatically; raw-count provenance
remains
the caller's responsibility. Alternative-experiment cell naming follows SCE's
own construction rules, so check alignment when constructing that object too.

External guide calls are a separate, explicit preparation operation. Configure
the analysis first, then supply a binary guide-by-original-cell matrix.
All-zero
columns mean unassigned cells; overlapping guides remain overlapping calls.
The usual low-MOI QC removes zero/multiple-guide cells. In multi-guide vector
screens, import sums counts by `vector_id`, as in ordinary SCEPTRE import;
external calls must then use those canonical **vector** IDs, with
caller-defined
vector-level calling rules. Individual guide calls are never silently
collapsed.

```{r analyze-export-sce}
target <- x$grna_target_data_frame$grna_target[1L]
pairs <- data.frame(grna_target = target, response_id = rownames(sce)[1L])
object <- set_analysis_parameters(object, discovery_pairs = pairs,
    formula_object = ~ log(response_n_umis), control_group = "complement",
    resampling_approximation = "no_approximation", side = "left")
# Transparent demonstration caller, not a universal recommended threshold.
calls <- x$grna_matrix >= 5
object <- set_grna_assignments(object, calls, "example caller: raw UMI >=5")
object <- run_qc(object, response_n_umis_range = c(0, 1),
    response_n_nonzero_range = c(0, 1), p_mito_threshold = 1,
    n_nonzero_trt_thresh = 3L, n_nonzero_cntrl_thresh = 3L)
object <- run_discovery_analysis(object, print_progress = FALSE)
returned <- export_results_to_sce(object, sce)
S4Vectors::metadata(returned)$sceptre$results$run_discovery_analysis
```

The wide QC ranges above keep the worked example simple; choose and report QC
thresholds appropriate to your experiment. Assignment validity is not
established
by successful import. Evaluate the upstream caller scientifically and run a
calibration check for the intended analysis. External calling does not alter
SCEPTRE's inference, multiplicity correction, defaults, or resampling budgets.

`set_grna_assignments()` rejects shuffled, missing or extra cell/guide IDs,
nonbinary values and missing provenance. It accepts calls independently of
guide
UMI thresholds and leaves the raw guide count library untouched. Repeating it
invalidates QC/results and applicable fit caches. Reconfigure parameters first
if necessary, then reapply external calls and QC. Inputs are copied by R's
normal
value semantics; results crossing the export boundary are explicitly owned.

Returned pair tables live in `metadata(returned)$sceptre`, with imported cell
covariates, original and retained cell IDs, assignment provenance,
schema/package
version and import identity. A response can be tested against multiple targets,
so putting one p-value in `rowData` would discard information. Export requires
exactly the original imported response counts and IDs, rejects stale or missing
results and existing `sceptre` metadata, and leaves the original SCE unchanged.
Save/reopen the returned object with `saveRDS()`/`readRDS()`.

For the schema-3 pipeline companion, serialize the configured, externally
assigned
object as the pipeline input. Keep `config$analysis` and `config$assignment`
absent (`NULL`) to preserve its preparation; the assignment stage checks
current
identity, including actual memberships and provenance. An explicit assignment
configuration requests reassignment; changing the analysis configuration
requires
reapplying external calls. A stale assignment fails before QC. Use the same
exact
candidate package in every pipeline process and regenerate the runtime lock.

The source tree includes an executable full roundtrip:

```{bash pipeline-sce, eval=FALSE}
R_LIBS=/absolute/isolated/library \
    Rscript tools/interoperability/sce-roundtrip.R \
    /absolute/schema3-pipeline-checkout /tmp/new-sce-roundtrip
```

It uses the full bundled 100-response, 1,000-cell example, launches the actual
pipeline stage CLI in separate R processes, compares pipeline/direct results at
tolerance zero, and writes `results-sce.rds` plus logs and dependency
identities.
This qualifies the pipeline's R-stage serialization/execution boundary; it is
not a scheduler or container qualification. See the separate Seurat
interoperability vignette for its optional adapter. AnnData, delayed-assay and
Python interfaces remain outside this supported slice.
